newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian central bank sees interest rates falling.
newsitem.headline: Croatian central bank sees interest rates falling.

text.p: Croatia's central bank sees interest rates falling this year after the January spread between commercial banks' deposit and lending rates dropped to the lowest level for 21 months.
"At 13.44 percent (spread) it quietly announces...a significant decrease in banks' credit rates," the central bank said in its March bulletin.
This was one of the main goals of this year's economic policy, the bulletin said.
Interest rates on kuna loans still differed considerably between banks, ranging from 9.8 percent to as high as 41.5 percent in January and fell to 17.62 from 18.46 percent.
The bank warned against blown up interest on the loans with a currency clause which rose to an average 20.08 percent in January from 18.97 percent in December.
"That category of credit continuously increases its weight in total banks' assets," the National Bank of Croatia said.
Commercial banks charged between 8.1 and 37.9 percent in January on loans with a currency clause.
Kuna credits represented 34.21 percent of the total commercial bank loan portfolio, and those with a currency clause accounted for almost 34 percent.
The January average deposit rate on kuna was 4.18 percent, compared to 4.15 a month earlier. The interest paid on currency deposits dropped to 4.51 from 5.09 percent in December 1996.
M1 money supply shrank 6.4 percent to 10.6 billion kuna in January while the total liquid assets measure, M4, rose 2.1 percent to 37.4 billion. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
